question.text: What will be the ending value of the UST 10Y Yield for these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 9 - Nov 20)
question.resolution_criteria: Each subquestion will resolve as the last available daily value of the U.S. Treasury Securities at 10-Year Constant Maturity published on the [FRED website](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10) for the final calendar day (typically the final Friday) of the corresponding biweekly period.
question.fine_print:
* If the FRED data is delayed, the value will be taken as soon as published for the relevant date.
* If the market is closed on the scheduled ending date or if no value for that date is published by FRED for two weeks, the most recent available value from an earlier day in the period will be used.
* Only the initially published value for each date will be used (no revisions).
* The value is reported in percentage points.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on FRED DGS10, the 10-year constant maturity yield, using the value for Friday 2026-11-20. That is a normal trading day. Wednesday 2026-11-11 is Veterans Day, so the bond market will be closed and FRED will publish no value for that date (it also showed none for Columbus Day, 2026-10-12). [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/DGS10.txt)
- The latest FRED value is 4.98 for 2026-10-29. Earlier closes: 10-28: 5.05, 10-27: 4.99, 10-26: 5.00, 10-23: 5.00, 10-22: 4.96, 10-21: 5.13, 10-19: 5.15, 10-14: 5.19, 10-09: 5.24, 10-05: 5.31 (the recent peak), 09-22: 4.96. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/DGS10.txt)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the outcome. The ending date is about three weeks away.
- 2026-11-02: market quotes put the 10-year at about 4.88-4.91% during the day, the lowest since mid-September. The prior close was about 4.93%. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield), [TradingView/TE](https://www.tradingview.com/news/te_news:597332:0-us-10-year-treasury-yield-lowest-in-8-weeks/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US10Y)
- 2026-10-30: about 4.93-4.94%, per a secondary source. FRED had not yet posted this date when I checked. [Vantage](https://www.vantagemarkets.com/market-analysis/why-dollar-index-fell-treasury-yields-usdx-analysis-november-2-6-2026/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Oil fell sharply: Brent dropped more than 3% to about $109-110, and Trading Economics cites a crude benchmark down about 7.8% to around $96. The drivers were US-Iran diplomacy hopes, Iran saying the Strait of Hormuz would fully reopen if conditions are met, and Rubio saying Trump prefers a diplomatic end to the Iran war. That eased inflation fears and pushed yields lower. [Cumhuriyet](https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/ekonomi/brent-petrol-109-dolara-geriledi-hurmuz-bogazi-iyimserligi-piyasalari-nasil-etkiledi-2552399), [Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/banks/government-bond-yields-log-best-session-since-april-as-crude-prices-slide-14066633.html), [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield)
- 2026-11-02: Futures still price about a 75% chance of a 25bp Fed **hike** in December. Other sources give between 60% and 85%. [TradingView/TE](https://www.tradingview.com/news/te_news:597332:0-us-10-year-treasury-yield-lowest-in-8-weeks/), [Avalon](https://avaloncapitalresearch.substack.com/p/weekly-playbook-futures-price-a-72)
- 2026-11-01: The 10-year fell about 33-36bp during October. [24/7 Wall St](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/01/the-10-year-treasury-yield-fell-33-basis-points-here-are-5-net-lease-reits-to-watch/)
- Late October: the Fed held rates at its October 28 meeting, with two dissents. Trading Economics gives the fed funds rate as 4.00%, but other reports differ. Recent data: September CPI 3.7% y/y (up from 3.4%), Q3 GDP 3.4% annualized, September PCE prices +0.5% m/m. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield)
- 2026-10-02: September payrolls rose only 29k and unemployment rose to 4.2%. [Invezz](https://invezz.com/en-ae/news/2026/10/02/us-jobs-report-payrolls-rise-just-29000-fed-october-hike-bets-fade/)

## 4. Base rates
- A code-computed baseline from FRED changes over 15 trading days since 2005, anchored at 4.98 on 10-29, gives: p5 4.66, p10 4.74, p25 4.86, p50 4.99, p75 5.12, p90 5.23, p95 5.31.
- Starting instead from about 4.89 on 11-02 (13-14 trading days to go), the same spread would shift down about 9bp, giving a median near 4.89-4.90.
- Recent volatility is high. Swings over 2-3 weeks of 15-35bp have been common lately: 5.31 on 10-05 to 4.96 on 10-22, and 4.96 on 09-22 to 5.29 on 09-30. One-day moves of 7-17bp have also occurred (10-21 to 10-22: -17bp).
- The trend is down from the 5.31 early-October peak. The yield is still about 0.76pp higher than a year ago.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi "10Y on Nov 2": about 58% for 4.88% or above, 31% for 4.90% or above. That implies a close of about 4.88-4.89.
- Kalshi November low (by Nov 30): about 51% for 4.76% or below, 62% for 4.80% or below.
- Kalshi November high: about 37% for 5.06% or above, 28% for 5.10% or above, 20% for 5.15% or above.
- Kalshi year-end (Dec 31): 69% for 4.75% or above, 47% for 5.00% or above, 34% for 5.25% or above, 10% for 5.50% or above.
- Kalshi "on Nov 3" and "on Nov 30": the listed prices are all 0.00, which looks like empty or illiquid books, so I would not rely on them.
- Polymarket "high before 2027": the 5.5% strike is at 8.8%.
- Trading Economics model: about 4.89% by end of Q4 and 4.68% in 12 months. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield)
- I could not find a contract that resolves on November 20 specifically.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (by 2026-11-20)
- 2026-11-03: US midterm elections. Commentators link control of Congress to how much room the administration has on Middle East policy and fiscal policy. [AA](https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/ekonomi/kuresel-piyasalar-onemli-gelismelerin-izlenecegi-haftaya-temkinli-basladi/4108294)
- 2026-11-06: October jobs report. Consensus is about 50-65k payrolls, 4.2% unemployment, and average hourly earnings +0.3% m/m. [Avalon](https://avaloncapitalresearch.substack.com/p/weekly-playbook-futures-price-a-72)
- 2026-11-10 (aggregator date, not confirmed on bls.gov): October CPI. [thriveinmarkets](https://thriveinmarkets.com/calendar/dates/cpi-2026/)
- 2026-11-11: Veterans Day, bond market closed.
- Mid-November: Treasury quarterly refunding auctions of 3-, 10- and 30-year debt, usually in the week of the 10th (I did not confirm the dates), plus PPI and retail sales releases.
- Ongoing: US-Iran talks over the Strait of Hormuz and the swings in oil prices. These have been the main driver of the inflation premium. Fed officials' comments ahead of the December FOMC will also matter.

Pulling it together now: the latest FRED value, recent news, the data calendar and market prices.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-29: The latest FRED DGS10 value is **4.98**. Readings just before it were 5.05 (10-28), 4.99 (10-27), 5.00 (10-26 and 10-23), 4.96 (10-22) and 5.13 (10-21). [FRED DGS10](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/DGS10.txt)
- The question resolves on the DGS10 value for Friday 2026-11-20, as first published. No US holiday falls on Nov 20. Veterans Day, Wed Nov 11, is a bond-market holiday, so FRED will have no value that day.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. It is 14 trading days from Nov 2 to Nov 20.
- 2026-10-30: FRED has not posted a value for this date yet. One undated report put the 10-year at about 4.925% after a tech sell-off. A third-party site shows a Treasury par yield of 4.94 for Oct 30. I could not confirm either figure from a primary source. [Finimize](https://finimize.com/content/techs-ai-spending-jitters-sent-investors-back-to-treasuries), [StockMarketWatch](https://stockmarketwatch.com/bonds/10-year-treasury-yield)
- 2026-11-02: The 10-year was at about 4.884% intraday, down more than 4bp. The 2-year was about 4.575% and the 30-year 5.253%. [CNBC](https://cnbc.com/2026/11/02/us-treasury-yields-bonds.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Oil fell after Secretary of State Rubio said Trump wants to end the Iran war "diplomatically". Brent dropped about 3% to roughly $109-110. Iran's foreign minister said the Strait of Hormuz would fully reopen if Washington's conditions are met. Yields were mixed. [CNBC](https://cnbc.com/2026/11/02/us-treasury-yields-bonds.html), [Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/banks/government-bond-yields-log-best-session-since-april-as-crude-prices-slide-14066633.html)
- 2026-11-02: CNBC says the close link between oil and yields seen earlier in the year faded in October as attention moved to AI and Big Tech. [CNBC](https://cnbc.com/2026/11/02/us-treasury-yields-bonds.html)
- 2026-10-30: A sell-off in megacap tech pushed investors into Treasuries, taking yields to about a one-month low. The 10-year was more than 40bp below its Oct 7 high, on track for the biggest monthly drop since December 2023. [The Edge](https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/824025)
- 2026-10-28: The Fed held rates at 3.75-4.00% on a 10-2 vote, with both dissenters (including Hammack) wanting a hike. CME FedWatch put the odds of a December hike at about 85%. The 10-year was at 5.05%. [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/28/business/live-news/federal-reserve-interest-rate-october)
- Background: September CPI inflation was reported at about 3.7% year on year. This comes from a secondary source (Trading Economics) and I did not verify it. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/interest-rate)

## 4. Base rates
- Recent trend: the 10-year rose from about 4.73 (2026-08-28) to a peak of 5.31 (10-05). It then fell to 4.96-5.05 in late October and is around 4.88-4.92 now. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/DGS10.txt)
- It has been volatile recently. Daily moves of 10-17bp happened several times, for example 10-21 to 10-22 (-17bp) and 9-22 to 9-23 (+15bp).
- The provided statistical baseline uses 15-period changes from the 4.98 of Oct 29. Its spread for Nov 20 runs from 4.66 (5th percentile) to 4.99 (median) to 5.31 (95th percentile), with an interquartile range of 4.86-5.12. If you re-center on about 4.89 for Nov 2, the median moves to roughly 4.89-4.90, with the 25th-75th percentile band at roughly ±13bp.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, Nov 2 close: 85% for 4.86% or above, 58% for 4.88% or above, 31% for 4.90% or above. That implies a close of about 4.88-4.89.
- Kalshi, November monthly low: 51% for touching 4.76% or below, 62% for 4.80% or below, 75% for 4.84% or below.
- Kalshi, November monthly high: 37% for touching 5.06% or above, 28% for 5.10% or above, 20% for 5.15% or above.
- Kalshi, year-end: 69% for 4.75% or above, 47% for 5.00% or above, 34% for 5.25% or above, 10% for 5.50% or above.
- Polymarket, highest level before 2027: 5.2% has already been hit; 5.5% is at 8.8%. The lowest-level market ("Below 4.0%" at 100%) is odd and looks unreliable.
- I found no Kalshi market for exactly Nov 20 and no consensus survey of bank forecasts for mid-November.

## 6. Upcoming events before Nov 20
- 2026-11-03: US midterm elections and September JOLTS. CNBC says the results matter for how much Congress plans to spend. [CNBC](https://cnbc.com/2026/11/02/us-treasury-yields-bonds.html)
- 2026-11-04: ADP employment and Treasury's quarterly refunding announcement (sizes of upcoming note and bond auctions). [CNBC](https://cnbc.com/2026/11/02/us-treasury-yields-bonds.html)
- 2026-11-05: Productivity and jobless claims.
- 2026-11-06: October jobs report, 8:30 ET. [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/11_sched_list.htm)
- About 2026-11-09 to 11-12: Likely 3-, 10- and 30-year auctions as part of the refunding (the usual pattern, not yet confirmed). The bond market is closed on Nov 11.
- 2026-11-10: October CPI, 8:30 ET. This is the key test for the December hike pricing. [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/11_sched_list.htm)
- 2026-11-13: October PPI. [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/11_sched_list.htm)
- Ongoing: US-Iran / Strait of Hormuz talks and oil prices (Brent still around $110), Apple and Qualcomm earnings this week and swings in AI/tech stocks driving safe-haven buying, and Fed speakers after the hawkish dissents.
